title: Synthetic and Masked Test Data: Coverage, Leakage, and Governance (2026)

questions.question: Eval data comes from production logs with user data and from public benchmarks the model may have memorized. What policy fixes both?
options: Use both sources as-is for speed
Trust public benchmarks blindly
Skip evals when data is inconvenient
Origin controls, anonymization, and leakage detection
questions.explanation: Convenient data leaks privacy; public data leaks answers. This lesson governs both before eval numbers mean anything.

questions.question: What threshold does k_anonymity_report use when the generated records are checked?
options: K=13, matching the n-gram size
K=0.30, matching the contamination threshold
K=0.05, matching the adversarial target
K=3, so each age_band/region group should contain at least three records
questions.explanation: K_ANONYMITY is 3. The report counts each generalised age and region pair and marks a group FAIL when its count is below three.

questions.question: When does classify_leakage label a non-exact record NGRAM_FLAG?
options: When its 13-gram contamination score is at least 0.30
When any single token appears in the training corpus
When its label is NEGATIVE or adversarial
When the record has fewer than 13 tokens
questions.explanation: For non-exact records, the classifier compares 13-gram overlap with NGRAM_THRESHOLD=0.30. Scores at or above the threshold become NGRAM_FLAG; lower scores remain CLEAN.

questions.question: Does generate_synthetic_records(n=18) meet the adversarial coverage target?
options: No; the generator creates only one adversarial record, below 5%
Yes; three of the 18 deterministic templates are adversarial, about 16.7%
No; adversarial records are excluded from coverage_report
Yes only when n is at least 100 because the target is an absolute count
questions.explanation: The template list contains three adversarial entries and 18 records are selected cyclically, giving 3/18 ≈ 16.7%. coverage_report compares that fraction with the 5% target.

questions.question: Why can an exact copy receive EXACT_MATCH even if its n-gram score would have been different?
options: 13-gram checks are disabled for all positive labels
The hash is used only for logging after the n-gram verdict
The fingerprint branch returns immediately with score 1.0 before n-gram scoring
Exact copies are always treated as CLEAN when they came from synthetic templates
questions.explanation: The exact fingerprint branch appends an EXACT_MATCH result and continues to the next record. It never reaches contamination_score for that record, so the reported score is exactly 1.0.

questions.question: What contamination score does contamination_score return for a non-exact record shorter than 13 tokens?
options: 1.0, because a short record is assumed to be copied
0.30, the configured threshold by default
An exception, because ngrams requires exactly 13 tokens
0.0, because ngrams produces no 13-gram tuples
questions.explanation: ngrams returns an empty set when the token list is shorter than NGRAM_N. contamination_score explicitly returns 0.0 for that empty record-ngram set.
